tools.source: interlock host tools go-duration-days --role worker --host claude-code

sessions.final_text:
`GetDuration` now accepts `d` as a unit of 24 hours, so `30d` reads as `720h0m0s`. interlock ran both checks on the final tree and both passed: `sh checks/days.sh` and `go test ./...`.

**Cause and fix:** `GetDuration` passed the value straight to `time.ParseDuration`, which has no day unit. It now calls a new `parseDuration` in `getters.go`, which handles a leading `d` and otherwise defers to `time.ParseDuration`. The input forms it accepts:
- **Old forms:** whole seconds (`90`) and Go syntax (`1m30s`) behave as before.
- **Day forms:** `30d`, `1.5d`, `-2d` and `1d12h` work.
- **Rejected:** `1h1d`, `1d-1h`, `1d5` and values too large to fit in a duration give an error.

I added `TestParseDurationDays` in `getters_test.go` and a sentence to `README.md`. The `repro` check is recorded as observed, and `regression` and `spec` as tested. `spec` still needs the independent verifier.

- **repro**: holds (observed). `sh checks/days.sh`, run by interlock on tree e30ae61, passes and prints `30d is 720h0m0s`.
- **spec**: holds (tested). A throwaway probe test, deleted afterwards and nothing left in the worktree, shows `30d`, `1.5d`, `-2d`, `1d12h` and `1d500ms` parse as days. `1h`, `1m30s`, `0`, `1h30m` and `-1h30m` give the same results as `time.ParseDuration`. Plain integers are still handled earlier in `GetDuration`. `1d1d`, `1D` and an overflowing day count return errors.
- **regression**: holds (tested). `go test ./...`, run by interlock on this tree, passes.

checks_run: interlock check run --criterion repro; interlock check run --criterion regression; git diff 3e6d67d --stat; git diff 3e6d67d -- getters.go

interlock assess add --criterion repro --strength observed --ref "interlock check run --criterion repro" --note "check passed on tree e30ae61: 30d is 720h0m0s"
interlock assess add --criterion spec --strength tested --ref "go test ./... plus probe test of parseDuration" --note "30d,1.5d,-2d,1d12h,1d500ms work; old forms (1h,1m30s,0,1h30m,-1h30m) identical to time.ParseDuration; integers handled earlier; bad forms (1d1d,1D,huge d) error. Tests pass."
interlock assess add --criterion regression --strength tested --ref "interlock check run --criterion regression" --note "go test ./... passes on tree e30ae61"
